a. MIDEST (Mining, raw materials)
b. WIDEST (waste, recycling, urban mining)

d. AIDEST (Architecture Investment Design)

f. HRDEST (Human Resource Design)
Through the six areas, we can create innovative overall concepts in master plans that consider various innovation aspects in context. Investor partners receive the necessary clear overview of the project parameters, qualities and quantities.

MSAO EST ensures a reliable investment policy combined with innovation diplomacy. 
MSAO has extensive experience in the negotiation, development and design of large regional, industrial and infrastructure projects. We are partners for governments in Germany and abroad. As architects and engineers, we combine design and technology to create innovation projects with visionary appeal as state-of-the-art projects.

entityDescription:
HUN-REN Research Centre for Natural Sciences (HUN-REN RCNS) is an organisational unit of HUN-REN Hungarian Research Network (a legal entity performing a public service function with a special legal status) and has a legal personality of its own. As a non-profit organisational unit of HUN-REN, RCNS qualifies as a research institution (a research and knowledge dissemination organisation), conducting multidisciplinary research in the natural sciences, including both the life sciences and the physical sciences. HUN-REN RCNS is entitled to apply for grants in its own name as well as receive grant funding and enter into contracts.
The HUN-REN Research Centre for Natural Sciences carries out multidisciplinary research in natural sciences in the fields of cognitive neuroscience and psychology, enzymology, organic chemistry, as well as materials- and environmental chemistry. Research Centre for Basic psychological research is performed both for pure scientific purposes and for direct or indirect application in Hungary. Research areas cover social, comparative cultural, cognitive and developmental psychology and psychophysiology. Research takes a broad approach to scientific issues, and embraces other branches of science and social science. Research centre staff is also engaged in adapting and developing new psychological research methods. Vocational and basic education at both undergraduate and postgraduate level is another area where research centre staff is active.

In the case of air vehicles will enable them to operate where aircraft are currently limited, increasing manoeuvrability by more than 50% and allowing them to operate in conditions of low or no speed and short takeoffs. In the Precision Agriculture sector, it sells software for the reduction and optimal recommendation in applying fertilisers using automatic learning models, improving the sustainability and yield of crops. Today, we are in Europe, South America and North Africa. Experts, universities and research institutions validate our services. RespiQ (Respiro B.V) is a company founded in 2019 with the aim to develop a hand held universal analyzer for chemical characterization of gases. RespiQ is now focused on the development of a breath analizer for the early detection of respiratory diseases and for the aid of chronic patients that suffer from diseases such as lung cancer, COPD and cystic fibrosis. The device developed is based on glow discharge, where the photons emitted by the breakage of the molecules are measured with a spectrometer. The spectrometer measures the intensity and wavelength of the photons and thanks to machine learning algorithms we will be able to determine the concentration and molecule or chemical identity. The molecular identity will then be related to a certain disease and a prognosis.
While the development of the breath analyzer is focused on medical applications, we are aware that the applications of the technology could every useful in space and environmental monitoring applications. The main advantage of this patented technology is the portability, sensitivity and simplicity, while keeping the costs low. Currently we have a working prototype that we are aiming to increase its sensitivity.
Recently, we have been awarded several European and local grants including a Eurostars and EIC project (4 Million Eur) to continue the development of our technology. We are aiming at developing this technology further and we are looking for a potential collaboration with ESA given the environment where this technology could be potentially used (atmospheric readings, space probes, rovers).
